_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) after at least two lines of systemic therapy, including a BTK inhibitor.

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, international, single-arm, multicenter study of pirtobrutinib as monotherapy.
pivotal_trials.population: 120 adult patients with MCL previously treated with a BTK inhibitor; median 3 prior lines (range 1-9), 93% having received 2 or more prior lines; median age 71 years.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) assessed by an independent review committee (IRC) using 2014 Lugano criteria.
pivotal_trials.result: ORR 50% (95% CI: 41, 59) with CR 13% and PR 38%; median DOR 8.3 months (95% CI: 5.7, NE).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=15%) were fatigue (29%), musculoskeletal pain (27%), diarrhea (19%), edema (18%), dyspnea (17%), pneumonia (16%), and bruising (16%). Grade 3 or 4 laboratory abnormalities (>=10%) were neutrophil count decreased (16%), lymphocyte count decreased (15%), and platelet count decreased (14%).
target_moa: Pirtobrutinib is an orally administered, noncovalent (reversible) Bruton tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor with comparable inhibitory activity toward wild-type BTK and the acquired resistance mutant BTK C481S.

rems.type: The clinical review team does not recommend a REMS; safety issues can be adequately managed through appropriate labeling and routine post-marketing surveillance.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not presented to the Oncologic Drug Advisory Committee, as it did not raise significant efficacy concerns or new safety concerns.

description.text: Added new indication: treatment of adult patients with CLL/SLL who have received at least two prior lines of therapy including a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor (accelerated approval)

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” sNDA provides for a new indication: Jaypirca for the treatment of adult patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL) who have received at least two prior lines of therapy, including a BTK inhibitor and a BCL-2 inhibitor.

description.text: Converted accelerated approval to traditional approval for relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL previously treated with a covalent BTK inhibitor

citations.quote: - Confirmatory study for pirtobrutinib in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL)/ Small Lymphocytic Lymphoma (SLL) to support the conversion from accelerated approval to traditional approval.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) supported by durability of response (DOR), an endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

citations.quote: ORR supported by durability is an endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, but is not a direct measure of clinical benefit in this setting.

confirmatory_requirement.text: Confirmatory randomized trial (BRUIN MCL-321, NCT04662255) comparing pirtobrutinib to investigator's choice BTK inhibitor, required as PMR 4389-1 to verify clinical benefit.

citations.quote: The confirmatory trial intended to verify clinical benefit is the BRUIN MCL-321 trial (NCT04662255), a Phase 3 randomized study of pirtobrutinib vs. investigator's choice of BTK inhibitor (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, or zanubrutinib) in patients with previously treated, BTK inhibitor-naïve MCL.

4389-1 Complete a randomized clinical trial to obtain data on the clinical efficacy and safety of pirtobrutinib in patients with mantle cell lymphoma. The trial should compare pirtobrutinib monotherapy to an investigator's choice of approved BTK inhibitors in patients with mantle cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint should be progression-free survival as assessed by an independent review committee, with secondary endpoints that include overall survival and objective response rate.

basis.text: FDA granted Fast Track Designation on 04 December 2020 for pirtobrutinib for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed and refractory MCL who have received a prior BTK inhibitor.

citations.quote: 04 December 2020 – FDA granted Fast Track Designation for pirtobrutinib “the treatment of adult patients with relapsed and refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received a prior BTK inhibitor.”

orphan_indication.text: This drug product for this indication (MCL) has an orphan drug designation.

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation and the molecular target of your drug is not relevant to the growth or progression of a pediatric cancer, you are exempt from this requirement.

basis.text: The application received Priority review designation.

summary.text: JAYPIRCA received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 based on ORR and DOR from the single-arm BRUIN trial, with a required confirmatory randomized trial (BRUIN MCL-321) to verify clinical benefit. The application had Priority review, Fast Track Designation (granted December 2020), and orphan drug designation for MCL.

citations.quote: It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.500), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling Marketing of this drug product and related activities must adhere to the substance and procedures of the referenced accelerated approval regulations.

04 December 2020 – FDA granted Fast Track Designation for pirtobrutinib “the treatment of adult patients with relapsed and refractory mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received a prior BTK inhibitor.”

Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation and the molecular target of your drug is not relevant to the growth or progression of a pediatric cancer, you are exempt from this requirement.

requirement.text: PMR 4389-1: Complete a randomized clinical trial comparing pirtobrutinib monotherapy to investigator's choice of approved BTK inhibitors in MCL, with primary endpoint of progression-free survival by IRC (confirmatory trial to verify clinical benefit).

citations.quote: 4389-1 Complete a randomized clinical trial to obtain data on the clinical efficacy and safety of pirtobrutinib in patients with mantle cell lymphoma. The trial should compare pirtobrutinib monotherapy to an investigator's choice of approved BTK inhibitors in patients with mantle cell lymphoma. The primary endpoint should be progression-free survival as assessed by an independent review committee, with secondary endpoints that include overall survival and objective response rate.

requirement.text: PMR 4389-2: Conduct a study to characterize the longer-term safety of pirtobrutinib monotherapy at 200 mg daily in patients treated in Study 18001, with a minimum of 24 months of follow-up.

citations.quote: 4389-2 Conduct a study to characterize the longer-term safety of pirbotrutinib monotherapy, at a planned dose of 200 mg daily, in patients with hematologic malignancies treated in Study 18001. Characterize safety and exposure with a minimum of 24 months of follow-up.

requirement.text: PMR 4389-3: Conduct an integrated safety analysis to further characterize the risk of second primary malignancies with extended follow-up (minimum 5 years).

citations.quote: 4389-3 Conduct an integrated safety analysis of patients with hematologic malignancies treated with pirbotrutinib monotherapy at the 200 mg daily dose in clinical trials and from post-marketing reports to further

characterize the risk of second primary malignancies with extended follow-up. Patients enrolled in clinical trials should have 5 years minimum follow-up for development of second primary malignancies.
